rows.name: Amiodarone
rows.summary: 15 mg/min example; rate hazard above 25 mg/min
rows.reference: Below 25 mg/min: below the specific fast infusion penalty. The source example is 150 mg over 10 minutes = 15 mg/min. The native effect reference is 150 mg.
rows.caution: Above 25 to 90 mg/min: the modeled resistance drop increases, making hypotension more likely. Existing low pressure and esmolol make the overall response less forgiving.
rows.danger: 90 mg/min or more: the fast infusion penalty is fully expressed once its rate smoothing catches up. 2,200 mg accumulated also enters the separate torsades risk gate; that is not a daily allowance. Active amiodarone burden above 2,310 mg equivalent can trigger the family overdose syndrome.
rows.watch: Follow blood pressure, pulse and rhythm. Amiodarone does not treat torsades. Lowering the clamp does not immediately erase drug effect or cumulative exposure.
rows.peak: 10 s native peak; rate hazard builds over about 15 s and eases over about 35 s after reduction.

rows.name: Epinephrine, both vial strengths
rows.summary: 0.5–15 mcg/min rate effect; higher delivery can trigger arrhythmias
rows.reference: 0–0.5 mcg/min: below the added epinephrine heart rate drive onset. 0.5–15 mcg/min: that drive rises toward its full +50 BPM target adjustment. These are effect bands, not a universally safe titration range.
rows.caution: 15 mcg/min or more: the added rate drive has reached its cap, while arrhythmia burden can continue rising. The 1 mg native reference and 1 mg preparation example are not routine doses for a perfusing patient.
rows.danger: At default settings, infusion alone reaches the atrial tachycardia score at about 20 mcg/min and the SVT score at about 38.9 mcg/min. These are eased rates; pulse state, rhythm, heart rate and sustained exposure gates must also qualify. Prior bolus support can reach the score sooner.
rows.watch: Track pulse, rhythm, pressure, perfusion and the exact access site. The 1 mg/mL and 0.1 mg/mL stocks deliver the same drug; confirm which vial is selected before drawing.
rows.peak: 5 s native peak; pressor delivery response ramps over about 45 s and fades over about 120 s.

rows.name: Norepinephrine
rows.reference: 0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/min is the source’s starting titration band: 4.15–8.3 mcg/min at 83 kg. The native effect reference is only 80 mcg; 4 mg is an amount used to prepare a bag.
rows.caution: Below that band: less support may be sufficient, or pressure may remain inadequate. Above it: you are beyond the starting band, not automatically overdosed. Titrate to the patient’s response and restore missing volume.
rows.danger: No universal toxic mcg/min cutoff is implemented. Pressure overshoot, worsening perfusion and extravasation remain reasons to reassess or reduce delivery. The default added MAP support cap is 25 mmHg before physiological gates; more drug does not guarantee more useful support. The configured 1 mg maxDose field is not a working norepinephrine overdose syndrome.
rows.watch: Reassess pressure, perfusion, volume, calcium, temperature and acidosis. A distal site does not turn norepinephrine into epinephrine; actual leakage still causes local injury.
rows.peak: 30 s native peak; pressor response ramps over about 45 s and fades over about 120 s.

rows.name: Lidocaine
rows.summary: Toxicity proxy: seizure 12, cardiac 15, arrest 25 mcg/mL
rows.reference: 83 mg at 83 kg is one native IV effect reference, equivalent to 1 mg/kg. The preparation recipe uses 100 mg. A partial reference is a smaller current antiarrhythmic effect, not proof of a safe infusion rate.
rows.caution: Below 12 mcg/mL: below the separate seizure trigger, with less margin as the proxy rises. The model’s default steady level is rate ÷ clearance. Shock and esmolol reduce clearance, so an unchanged rate can accumulate further.
rows.danger: 12 mcg/mL: seizure trigger unless suppressed; 15 mcg/mL: cardiac toxicity begins; 25 mcg/mL: bradyasystolic arrest threshold. With normal 0.40 L/min clearance, the corresponding steady rates are 4.8, 6 and 10 mg/min. With both shock and esmolol, they fall to about 2.02, 2.52 and 4.2 mg/min. These are eventual plateaus, not instant rate triggers or recommended doses.
rows.watch: Watch rhythm, pressure, breathing and seizure activity. Prior boluses change the starting level. Controlling a seizure does not remove lidocaine or prevent cardiac toxicity.
rows.peak: 5 s native peak; the independent accumulation proxy follows distribution and clearance.

rows.name: Ketamine
rows.summary: Analgesia 0.1–0.2 mg/kg IV; induction about 1.75 mg/kg
rows.reference: 0.1–0.2 mg/kg IV/IO spans the native analgesic anchors: 8.3–16.6 mg at 83 kg. At full effect, ketamine alone reaches the default induction level near 1.75 mg/kg, or 145.25 mg at 83 kg.
rows.caution: Between analgesia and induction: analgesia and hypnosis change separately. Repeated doses and an infusion add to the same current exposure. A 50 mg bag recipe is neither an induction requirement nor a maximum.
rows.danger: Extra respiratory depression begins above 1.6 induction equivalents, about 2.8 mg/kg IV at full effect, and increases toward 3.2 equivalents. The family overdose evaluator can trigger above 262.5 mg of active IV-equivalent ketamine alone; IM ketamine and esketamine also contribute through their own thresholds. Shock, rapid IV pushes and combinations can cause problems below that total.
rows.watch: Reassess breathing, pressure and actual sedation. See Ventilator Settings & Tips for the nystagmus finding. Rocuronium contributes no sedation.
rows.peak: 5 s IV/IO native peak. Sedation depends on current combined effect, not merely time since the syringe was pushed.

rows.name: Tranexamic acid (TXA)
rows.summary: 0–1 g builds toward the native 1 g reference
rows.reference: 0–1 g delivered: builds toward one native medication reference as the dose takes effect. 1 g is the preparation example and effect reference; it describes a finite hemorrhage adjunct.
rows.caution: Beyond 1 g: more delivered drug and carrier do not replace pressure, packing, blood replacement or other bleeding control. Account for earlier TXA doses before adding another bag.
rows.danger: No dedicated high-dose toxicity threshold or safe maintenance rate is implemented in the reviewed TXA path. Do not read that absence as an unlimited safe range. This wiki does not assign an invented red cutoff or a continuous treatment schedule.
rows.watch: Track total delivered amount, remaining bleeding and the need for further treatment. Close the clamp when the intended finite amount has been delivered.
rows.peak: 15 s native peak for an admitted reference amount.

rows.name: Fentanyl
rows.summary: 0.5–1 mcg/kg reference band; opioid burden can become toxic
rows.reference: 0.5–1 mcg/kg IV/IO spans the native analgesic anchors: 41.5–83 mcg at 83 kg. The 100 mcg recipe amount is the bag’s content example, not a guaranteed safe exposure.
rows.caution: Above 110 mcg of active IV-equivalent exposure can satisfy the native instability check when heart rate is below 50. Respiratory depression and loss of CO₂ response can matter before an overdose syndrome appears.
rows.danger: Fentanyl alone can trigger the opioid overdose evaluator above 157.5 mcg of active IV-equivalent exposure. Morphine, IM fentanyl and the lozenge add to the same normalized family burden; do not add their raw mg together. Sedatives increase respiratory risk below this threshold.
rows.watch: Follow ventilation and consciousness as well as pain. Opioids are analgesic adjuncts; they do not provide reliable hypnosis by themselves. Naloxone reverses opioid effects, but reassessment remains necessary.
rows.peak: 10 s IV/IO native peak; effect can persist after the line stops.

rows.name: Morphine
rows.summary: 0.05–0.1 mg/kg reference band; combined opioid risk
rows.reference: 0.05–0.1 mg/kg IV/IO spans the native analgesic anchors: 4.15–8.3 mg at 83 kg. The preparation example contains 10 mg.
rows.caution: Above 10 mg of active IV-equivalent exposure can satisfy the native instability check when heart rate is below 50. Pressure and respiratory response still need reassessment below that amount.
rows.danger: Morphine alone can trigger the opioid overdose evaluator above 12.6 mg of active IV-equivalent exposure. Fentanyl and other opioid routes reduce the remaining family margin. Propofol or midazolam add respiratory and pressure depression.
rows.watch: Follow pain, pressure, breathing and current opioid exposure. A partly empty bag does not show how much active medication remains in the patient.
rows.peak: 25 s IV/IO native peak; 1,300 s native duration.

rows.name: Midazolam
rows.summary: 5 mg native reference; about 10 mg alone reaches default induction
rows.reference: 0–5 mg current IV equivalent: builds toward one native reference. 5 mg contributes about half an induction equivalent; 10 mg alone reaches one equivalent at full effect with default tuning.
rows.caution: Above 5–10 mg, or when combined with another sedative: hypnosis, respiratory depression and pressure effects accumulate. Propofol and opioids amplify the combined response. Allow for its slower peak before repeating.
rows.danger: No universal mg/min danger threshold is wired for midazolam. Its 20 mg unstableDose and 30 mg maxDose config fields do not establish a functioning, separate IV overdose gate in the reviewed handlers. Loss of breathing or deteriorating pressure is dangerous at any dose.
rows.watch: Check ventilator delivery, CO₂, spontaneous effort, sedation and pressure. Muscle paralysis can hide movement without treating awareness.
rows.peak: 240 s IV native peak; a long effect tail follows delivery.

rows.name: Ondansetron
rows.summary: 4 mg reference; conditional instability above 8 mg
rows.reference: 0–4 mg current IV equivalent: builds toward one native nausea-treatment reference. The preparation example contains 4 mg.
rows.caution: 4–8 mg: greater exposure is not automatically greater symptom relief. It does not reverse opioid respiratory depression or replace reassessment of the cause of vomiting.
rows.danger: Above 8 mg of active IV-equivalent exposure with HR below 50 can satisfy the native instability check. There is no separate ondansetron overdose syndrome in the supported overdose handler and no validated safe continuous rate in this model.
rows.watch: Reassess nausea, vomiting, pulse and other medications. Treat it as an indicated finite administration rather than a routine indefinite drip.

rows.name: Calcium chloride
rows.summary: Accumulation and fast delivery both matter; 1 g reference
rows.reference: 1 g is the native replacement reference. One slow arithmetic example is 1 g over 10 min = 100 mg/min of calcium chloride, or 27.3 mg/min elemental calcium. The model’s elemental fraction is 0.273.
rows.caution: Sustained delivery above about 219.8 mg/min of the salt can eventually exceed the modeled excess-calcium threshold, even before a fast-rate penalty appears. This derives from 60 mg/min elemental calcium and assumes no previous excess. Stop when the intended replacement is delivered.
rows.danger: Fast-rate toxicity begins above about 366.3 mg/min of salt and reaches full depth near 1,025.6 mg/min. Independently, the excess-calcium proxy enters toxicity above 1 mg/dL and reaches full depth at 4 mg/dL. The worse of the rate and accumulation effects applies; severe bradycardia and arrest are possible.
rows.watch: Track cumulative calcium, transfusion context, pressure, rhythm and IV site integrity. Calcium gluconate adds to the same elemental calcium burden. This is not the patient’s measured total serum calcium.
rows.peak: 300 s native effect peak; toxicity has its own rate and accumulation timing.

rows.name: Calcium gluconate
rows.summary: 3 g reference; shares calcium toxicity with calcium chloride
rows.reference: 3 g gives about 1 g of CaCl₂-equivalent replacement credit. Over 10 min, that is 300 mg/min of gluconate, or 27.9 mg/min elemental calcium. The elemental fraction is 0.093.
rows.caution: Sustained delivery above about 645.2 mg/min of the salt can eventually exceed the modeled excess-calcium threshold from a zero starting excess. The gentler salt does not remove the shared accumulation risk.
rows.danger: Fast-rate toxicity begins above about 1,075.3 mg/min of salt and reaches full depth near 3,010.8 mg/min. The same excess-calcium thresholds apply: above 1 mg/dL enters toxicity, and 4 mg/dL reaches full depth. Previous calcium chloride or gluconate reduces the remaining margin.
rows.watch: Use the correct salt concentration and count both salts. Reassess rhythm, pressure and site leakage; replacement credit and elemental toxicity use different conversions.
rows.peak: 420 s native effect peak; toxicity uses a separate accumulator.

rows.name: Ceftriaxone
rows.summary: 0–1 g builds toward the native antibiotic reference
rows.reference: 0–1 g delivered: builds toward the 1 g game reference as effect develops. The preparation example uses 10 mL from the 100 mg/mL stock.
rows.caution: Beyond the intended finite amount: additional bag content is not evidence that more antibiotic is required. The game retains ceftriaxone’s identity while using the shared antibiotic-care abstraction.
rows.danger: No dedicated ceftriaxone overdose cutoff or safe ongoing infusion rate is implemented in the reviewed path. The generalized debug concentration band is display-only and must not be presented as a toxicity boundary.
rows.watch: Track the amount actually delivered and the treatment indication. Continue the underlying trauma and evacuation plan.
rows.peak: 5 s native IV/IO reference peak; not a prediction of real antibiotic response time.

rows.name: Propofol
rows.summary: 100 mg at 83 kg is one induction reference; pressure risk rises with exposure
rows.reference: 0–100 mg at 83 kg spans zero to one native effect equivalent. At full effect, 100 mg alone gives one induction equivalent; the reference scales with body weight.
rows.caution: More than one reference, or mixed sedatives: hypnosis and respiratory depression increase. Opioids and midazolam can achieve a given hypnotic effect with less propofol while adding respiratory and pressure risk.
rows.danger: No universal safe mg/min limit or separate propofol overdose trigger is defined here. The 200 mg unstableDose and 400 mg maxDose fields are not functioning standalone propofol gates in the reviewed handlers. Hypovolemia and acidosis worsen the pressure response; apnea or hypotension can occur below those numbers.
rows.watch: Follow delivered ventilation, CO₂, pressure and sedation. Supply analgesia separately when required. Avoid treating a motionless, paralyzed patient as proof of adequate hypnosis.
rows.peak: 90 s IV/IO native peak; 480 s native duration.

rows.name: Esmolol premix
rows.summary: Steady reference 1.75–7 mg/min; toxicity rises above 2 mcg/mL
rows.reference: The modeled display band is 0.5–2 mcg/mL. At default clearance, its steady input equivalent is 1.75–7 mg/min, or 10.5–42 mL/h of the 10 mg/mL premix. This is a game reference band, not proof of safe perfusion.
rows.caution: Above 7 to 17.5 mg/min, a constant infusion can eventually settle in the 2–5 mcg/mL toxicity band. A previous bolus changes the starting level. Native rate control and this accumulation model are separate.
rows.danger: Above 2 mcg/mL: increasing bradycardia and hypotension. 5 mcg/mL or higher: full modeled overdose depth. A steady 17.5 mg/min reaches that plateau, but not immediately. The full 2.5 g bag is inventory content, not an administration target.
rows.watch: Follow pulse, pressure and rhythm. Amiodarone adds nodal and pressure depression; esmolol also reduces lidocaine clearance.
rows.peak: 20 s native peak. Accumulation follows distribution and clearance, rather than an immediate rate cutoff.

rows.name: Magnesium sulfate premix
rows.summary: 2 g over 5–10 min example; rate hazard above 800 mg/min
rows.reference: The native reference is 2 g. The source’s example range is 200–400 mg/min, equivalent to a 2 g dose over 10–5 min. At 40 mg/mL, this is 300–600 mL/h for a finite bag.
rows.caution: Above 800 to 2,500 mg/min: the fast infusion penalty rises, suppressing heart rate and reducing resistance. Below 800 mg/min only means this particular fast-rate penalty has not started.
rows.danger: 2,500 mg/min or more: full fast-rate penalty after smoothing. Excessively fast delivery can worsen bradycardia and pressure. The generic 2–4 mg/dL debug band is display-only; it is not the trigger for these effects.
rows.watch: For torsades, enough native effect must develop before a termination attempt. Continue arrest care and correct causes; a bag being attached is not proof that a therapeutic amount reached the patient.
rows.peak: 90 s native peak; fast-rate penalty builds over about 15 s.

rows.name: Hypertonic saline 3%
rows.summary: 250 mL reference; benefit stops at the sodium ceiling
rows.reference: 0–250 mL spans zero to the osmotherapy reference volume, containing up to 7.5 g NaCl. At default settings, 250 mL can lower the ICP proxy by up to 8 mmHg and add 3 mEq/L to the sodium proxy, subject to its floors and ceiling.
rows.caution: Repeated volumes: add sodium and consume the remaining sodium margin. The full bag is a calibration amount, not an instruction to empty it. Benefits depend on the current ICP and retained TBI state.
rows.danger: Sodium at or above 160 mEq/L by default: further osmotherapy stops lowering ICP. The setting can be changed. The reviewed path does not define a separate universal dangerous mL/min or total-volume cutoff; the ceiling is a loss-of-benefit boundary, not a promise that lower values are safe.
rows.watch: Follow neurological findings, perfusion, delivered volume and the exact site. HTS extravasation is a local tissue hazard. It is not routine volume-resuscitation crystalloid.
rows.peak: Osmotherapy follows actual admitted volume, not a native medication peak curve.

rows.name: Mannitol 20%
rows.summary: 500 mL / 100 g reference; no fixed overdose volume in this path
rows.reference: 0–500 mL spans zero to the default osmotherapy reference, or 0–100 g at 200 mg/mL. The full reference can lower the ICP proxy by up to 8 mmHg while the model permits benefit.
rows.caution: Repeated volumes: cannot drive ICP below its treatment floor. Mannitol’s configured sodium increment is zero, unlike HTS, but an already reached sodium ceiling still blocks this osmotherapy path.
rows.danger: No standalone safe-to-dangerous dose or rate boundary is implemented for mannitol in this path. Do not turn the 100 g bag total into a routine dose or an unlimited repeat allowance. Reassess low pressure, volume state and leakage instead of chasing the ICP number with another bag.
rows.watch: Track perfusion, volume, neurological findings and site integrity. Keep the ongoing injury and its recovery requirements in view after a temporary ICP improvement.
rows.peak: Effect follows admitted volume through the separate osmotherapy model.
